'''2001 Montreal DPC''' was a constructed Star Wars CCG Decipher Player Championship on 18 August 2001 in Montreal, Quebec. About 42 players came. With fewer than 60, the prize support was scaled down to a Master's event.<ref name="tr-chu">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-08-19-dpc-montreal-8-18-01d2868/ dpc-montreal-8-18-01], Jonathan "jonnychu" Chu, DeckTech (19 August 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-08-19-dpc-montreal-8-18-01d2868/ GitHub Pages].</ref> Eight Swiss rounds cut to a final four. [[Yannick Lapointe]] won, beating [[Jonny Chu]] in the final.<ref name="tr-chu" /><ref name="tr-gog">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-09-15-montreal-dpc-from-the-overall-1st-placed2963/ montreal-dpc-from-the-overall-1st-place], Chris "CGogolen" Gogolen, DeckTech (15 September 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-09-15-montreal-dpc-from-the-overall-1st-placed2963/ GitHub Pages].</ref> [[Chris Gogolen]] finished the Swiss first and lost his semifinal to Lapointe.<ref name="tr-gog" />

* '''Dates:''' 18 August 2001
* '''Site:''' Montreal, Quebec
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Coruscant]]
* '''Winner:''' [[Yannick Lapointe]]

Gogolen went 4–0 with his Light list and 3–1 with his Dark list in the Swiss. His one loss was a true-tie time loss.<ref name="dt-18785" /><ref name="dt-18784" /> Gogolen played the same two decks at the [[2001 DragonCon Open]] two weeks later.<ref name="dt-18785" /> [[Andy Klema]] went 4–0 with his Light list and 5–3 overall.<ref name="dt-19025" /><ref name="tr-klema" /> Michael Gemme and Brian Twigg each went 3–1 with the same Dark list.<ref name="dt-18484" /> [[Thomas Dowling]] went 5–1 across the warm-up and the DPC, losing to Chris Terwilliger.<ref name="dt-18473" />

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on this page, the page keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* The hub lists Thomas Dowling with a '5–1 record (warm-up and DPC combined)' from his deck post; that is his Light deck's record. His report gives 3–1 at the warm-up and 5–3, 10 (−9), at the DPC.<ref name="tr-d2869">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-08-19-dpc-montreal-roadtrip-cotebs-viewd2869/ dpc-montreal-roadtrip-cotebs-view], DeckTech (Thomas "COTEB" Dowling, 19 August 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-08-19-dpc-montreal-roadtrip-cotebs-viewd2869/ GitHub Pages].</ref>
